The Kukama Kukamiria, or Kokama, are an Indigenous people of the Peruvian Amazon, on the lower Marañón, Ucayali and Huallaga rivers and the Amazon itself, with communities also in Brazil and Colombia. Their language is Tupi-Guarani and closely related to that of the Omagua.

They were river people who fished and farmed the floodplains and travelled by canoe. In the 1600s Jesuit missions of Maynas reached them, and over time they mixed with Spanish speakers and other peoples. The rubber boom brought hard labour around 1900. Today few young people speak the language, and the Kokama have worked to revive it. Their neighbours include the Ticuna and the Yagua.
